title.en: AP Calculus AB Exam Format & Units Overview

body.en: AP Calculus AB Exam Format & Units Overview covers essential College Board AP Calculus AB competencies across foundational mechanics, intermediate analysis, and advanced FRQ problem solving.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Exam Blueprint & 8 Curriculum Units

body.en: Master the 8 core units of AP Calculus AB and the point distribution across Section I Multiple Choice and Section II Free Response.

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

How many total questions are on the AP Calculus AB exam, and what percentage of the composite score comes from Free-Response questions?

solution.en: The exam consists of 45 Multiple-Choice Questions and 6 Free-Response Questions (51 total). Free Response accounts for exactly 50% of the composite score (54 out of 108 scaled points).

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Unit Weighting & Calculator Policy Transitions

body.en: Unit 4/5 (Applications of Derivatives) and Unit 6/8 (Integration) combine to represent over 55% of the exam questions.

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

During Section I Part B (Calculator), what are the four required calculator capabilities that College Board assesses?

solution.en: The four required graphing calculator capabilities are: 1. Graphing a function within an arbitrary viewing window; 2. Finding the zeros (roots) of a function; 3. Computing the numerical derivative of a function; 4. Computing the numerical definite integral of a function.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Composite Score Scaling & The 5-Score Threshold

body.en: College Board scaling typically sets a score of approximately 65–70 out of 108 raw points (~62%) as the threshold for a score of 5.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

If a student earns 32 out of 45 points on Section I and 34 out of 54 points on Section II, what is their composite score out of 108?

solution.en: Multiple Choice is scaled by 1.2: \(32 \times 1.2 = 38.4\). Free Response points count 1:1: \(34 \times 1 = 34\). Total composite score: \[ 38.4 + 34 = \mathbf{72.4\text{ out of 108 points}}, \] which safely earns an AP score of 5.
